doc:
Biology 2024 Higher Level, deferred sitting: reviewed task ledger, carded for the first time.

Independent visual sweep (2026-11-19), every page rendered and read:
  * LC025ALP038EV (deferredexams/2024; Sections A and B and Answerbook), 40 pages: p1 cover, p2
    instructions, p3-p9 Section A Questions 1-7, p10-p12 Section B Questions 8-10, p13 Section C
    answerbook instructions, p14-p15 graph paper, p16-p39 ruled answer pages, p40 back cover.
  * LC025ALP040EV (Section C), 12 pages: p1 cover, p2-p10 Questions 11-17, p11 "Do not hand this
    question paper up", p12 back cover.
  * LC025ALP000EV (deferredmarkingschemes/2024), 32 pages: p1 cover, p2 the deferred-scheme note, p3
    introduction, p4-p5 marking examples, p6 the annotations table, p7-p31 Questions 1-17, p32 back cover.

The sitting has the June shape (any five of Section A, any two of B, any four of C). The deferred scheme
sets out every printed ask, so no card needs the "prints no answer" row. Tariffs as the scheme prints
them: Q1 best five of six at 4 (Q1(c), (d) "any three" elements are one 4-mark answer each); Q2-Q4, Q6
and Q7 one ladder each, 6(3) + 2; Q5 3(2) + 4(3) + 2; Section B and C rows carry the scheme's own marks
under each part's "Number of correct responses" table; Q16 and Q17 parts at 30. Q2's ticks are read from
their positions (two glyphs overprint (f)'s True box; the upper is read). Q5(a)(ii)'s three parts are read
from their own column by glyph position, the tariff printed beside them interleaving the text layer.
Drawings are criterion rows priced as printed, labels 1 each. Numbered asks (Q11(b)(iii)1-2,
Q12(b)(ii)1-2, Q12(b)(iii)1-3, Q12(c)(ii)1-2, Q14(b)(v)1-2, Q14(c)(iii)1-2, Q15(b)(iii)1-2,
Q15(b)(iv)1-2, Q15(c)(iv)1-2, Q16(a)(iv)1-2, Q16(b)(ii)1-4, Q16(c)(ii)1-2, Q16(c)(iv)1-3,
Q17(c)(ii)1-3, Q17(c)(iii)1-2) are priced separately and carded one each.
SELECTION_SCAN: Instructions: "blue or black pen", not a question.
Section A rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Section B rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Section C rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Q1 best five of (a)-(f): each part is its own card at 4.
Q1(c) "any three elements": one 4-mark answer; one card.
Q1(d) "any three elements": one 4-mark answer; one card.
Q2 "true or false": the answer options.
Q5(a)(ii) "any two of the parts X, Y, and Z": bounded menu of parts; one card.
Q6(f)(i) "any one abiotic factor": open single answer; one card.
Q6(f)(ii) "any one abiotic factor": open single answer; one card.
Q8(b)(iii) "any two" collection methods: both required on the scheme's rows; one card.
Q10(b) "a sheep's or an ox's heart": the material, not a choice of task.
Q10(b)(vi) "the following: septum, right ventricle, left atrium": every label asked; one card.
Q12(a): every term asked, one card each.
Q12(b)(ii)2 "any one conservation practice": open single answer; one card.
Q12(b)(ii)2 "mentioned in the passage, or from one of the following areas": source of the answer; one card.
Q12(c)(ii)1 "from one of the following areas": open choice of area; one card.
Q14(b)(iii) "both fertilisations": both products required; one card.
Q14(b)(iv) "labelling the following parts": every label asked; one card.
Q14(c)(i) "any two of these factors": bounded menu; one card.
Q14(c)(iii) lead-in "either asexual ... or sexual": description, both items asked.
Q16 "any two of (a), (b), (c), (d)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q16(a)(iv)1 "label the following parts": every label asked; one card.
Q16(d)(i) "Label the following parts": every label asked; one card.
Q16(d)(ii) "enter or exit": description, not a choice.
Q17 "any two of (a), (b), (c), (d)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q17(a)(i) "any two parts": bounded menu; one card.
Q17(c)(ii) "each of the following endocrine glands": each gland asked, one card per item.
Q17(c)(iii) lead-in: every item asked, one card each.
Q17(d)(ii) "Choose one of the parts": open choice; the scheme answers each part; one card.
Q17(d)(iv) "label the following parts": every label asked; one card.

q3-enzyme: Ribbon diagram of an enzyme: a folded chain shown as coils and arrows, with a pocket in its surface labelled Active site.
q4-dna: Diagram of a piece of DNA: a ladder of base pairs (A = T, G ≡ C) in the lower part, and at the top the two strands drawn apart, single bases lined up beside each separated strand.
q5-skin: Diagram of a vertical section of human skin: X points to a hair, Y to a coiled gland deep in the skin, and Z to a vessel below the surface; the Sebaceous gland beside the hair is labelled.
q6-pyramids: Two pyramids of numbers. Terrestrial ecosystem: Rose at the base, Aphid above it, Ladybird above that and Spider at the top, the bars of very different widths. Aquatic ecosystem: Phytoplankton at the base, then Zooplankton, Herring and Sea lion, the bars narrowing upwards.
q7-bacteria: Electron microscope image of bacterial cells with many tiny virus particles attached to their surfaces.
q11-chromosomes: Chromosome diagrams of two parents: Parent 1 has an X chromosome carrying allele n and a Y chromosome; Parent 2 has two X chromosomes, one carrying N and one carrying n.
q13-greenhouse: Photograph of a large industrial greenhouse with rows of crops under glass.
q14-flower: Diagram of a typical flower with three structures labelled: Petal, Anther and Sepal.
q14-pollination: Photograph of an insect on a flower.
q15-nephron: Diagram of a nephron with its blood supply: a cup-shaped capsule around a knot of capillaries, a coiled tubule, a long loop, a second coiled tubule and a collecting duct.
q16-skull: Diagram of a human skull with the lines between its bones marked, one labelled Joint.
q16-phagocyte: Diagram of a phagocyte engulfing a bacterium.
q16-cycle: Diagram of the stages of the menstrual cycle in the ovary across days 1, 14 and 28: a Follicle growing in size, then releasing an egg, then a body labelled Structure A that later shrinks; Days 1, 14 and 28 are marked below.
q17-canal: Diagram of part of the alimentary canal: the large intestine framing the coiled small intestine, with the appendix, rectum and anus.
q17-mould: Photograph of bread with a fuzzy growth of mould on it, labelled Rhizopus.
q17-outline: Outline of a human body, front view.
q17-brain: Diagram of a cross section of the human brain: B points to the large folded upper part, C to the rounded part at the lower back, and A to the stem at the base.

Q.start: Explain in detail how any two of the parts X, Y, and Z help to regulate body

G.expect: X: When the body is cold the (hair) will stand on end (or piloerection) trapping a layer of air close to the skin and reduce heat loss or When the body is hot the (hairs) lie flat allowing more heat loss from the surface of the skin

Y: When the body is hot, the (sweat glands) produces and release sweat to the surface of the skin which evaporates and has a cooling effect on the body or When the body is cold, the (sweat glands) does not produce sweat no evaporation from the surface of the skin occurs so less heat is lost

Z: When the body is cold the (blood vessels) constrict (or become narrower) causing less blood flow to the surface of the skin and conserving heat or When the body is hot the (blood vessels) dilate (or become wider) causing more blood flow to the surface of the skin and releasing heat
